doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Irakere's first CBS records and a Grammy
summary: After the live recording they recorded Irakere, which won a Grammy, then Irakere II, when Lundvall proposed a solo LP, and CBS gave the group world exposure.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So, you made that live recording of that concert, and that was the first American or US exposure to the band, to Irakere. How did you come to make your first solo record for CBS?

Well, after that live recording, we came here, we came to New York, and then to Switzerland. When we came back we recorded the first numbers of Irakere. Is that the name of the LP, Irakere was a very nice album. And we won a Grammy for it, and then we did the second one; it was Irakere II and in that occasion Bruce Lundvall proposed me to record by myself, an LP by myself for CBS. So he kept that promise when I came back for good in 1980.
After the band made the first record for CBS, what did that exposure mean for Irakere? What did that do to help the band?

Well, CBS is a gigantic company. So, the resolution of that size company is that, is very impressive. Exposure is what’s very important in what’s working with a company like that. We received a world exposure that helped a lot to publicize the group, and very soon, the contribution of the group was recognized around the world.
